System description:
# Case: Tesla Model S with Autopilot (Williston, Florida, 2016)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-17/02. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2015 Tesla Model S has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings and objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, slows down for a vehicle ahead in the same lane, and speeds up again when the lane is clear.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle centered in its lane using lane markings and the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: the system checks that the driver's hands are on the steering wheel by sensing steering torque, and shows visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users include cars, large trucks crossing or joining the road, and motorcyclists.

## Operating context
Autopilot is intended mainly for highways with limited access, in good visibility. Drivers can also turn it on for other roads, such as divided highways with cross traffic at intersections.

requirements.text: The system shall classify a crossing or broadside truck detected by its sensors as a vehicle relevant to the Tesla’s path, regardless of its orientation, and shall not suppress the detection solely because classification is uncertain.
TACC shall reduce speed when a detected vehicle is predicted to intersect the Tesla’s path, even if that vehicle is not yet in the same lane.

When the system predicts a forward collision with a crossing vehicle, it shall issue a collision warning no later than 2.5 seconds before predicted impact, where the available sensor data supports that prediction.

When the system predicts an imminent collision with a vehicle crossing the Tesla’s path and the driver has not braked, automatic emergency braking shall apply braking within its declared operating limits.

While Autopilot is active, the system shall detect when the driver’s gaze is directed away from the road for more than 2 seconds and issue an alert; if the driver does not respond, it shall issue an escalating alert and disengage Autopilot safely.

Before enabling Autopilot, the system shall require the driver to acknowledge a clear statement that Autopilot is Level 2 assistance and the driver remains responsible for monitoring and control; it shall repeat this statement during use.

Steering torque alone shall not be treated as evidence that the driver is attentive; the system shall use a separate attention measure and shall alert when the driver is inattentive even if steering torque is present.
The system shall identify roads with at-grade cross traffic as outside its intended operating conditions and shall inhibit Autopilot on those roads or warn the driver and prevent continued use.
The system shall detect a vehicle crossing or joining the Tesla’s path without yielding and shall initiate available collision-mitigation actions, regardless of which road user has right of way.
TACC shall not accelerate toward the set speed when a detected vehicle is predicted to enter or obstruct the Tesla’s path within the next 5 seconds, even if the current lane is judged clear.
